question.text: SEBI's Cyber Security and Cyber Resilience Framework (CSCRF), 2024 (Circular dated August 20, 2024) applies to AIFs. A cyber-incident (data breach) occurs at Ashoka Credit AIF. What is the SEBI-mandated timeline for reporting to CERT-In?

answer.text: Within 6 hours of noticing or being brought to attention of the incident
Within 48 hours; only to SEBI, not CERT-In
Annually, in the Compliance Test Report

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the CERT-In directions (as incorporated in SEBI's CSCRF 2024), regulated entities including AIFs must report cyber incidents to CERT-In within 6 HOURS of noticing/being brought to attention. SEBI CSCRF classifies AIFs as qualified RE / mid-size RE / small-size RE / self-certification REs based on client count, AUM and trade volume — governance, tech committee, critical systems identification and reporting obligations flow accordingly. The Trap: Option B (30 days) is the annual audit cadence. Option C (48 hours) is an older RBI data-breach norm for banks. Option D (annual) is incorrect — cyber incidents are immediate-reporting events. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests CSCRF. XXIV AML and X-A Investment Adviser also reference CERT-In reporting. General IT Act 2000 Sec 70B governs CERT-In. Time-critical: train compliance team on 6-hour trigger. Manager's Pro-Tip: Maintain a cyber-incident runbook with 24x7 hotline to your SOC provider + CERT-In + SEBI regional office. Tag every incident (ransomware, phishing, unauthorised access) and keep templates pre-drafted. In SEBI inspections, absence of documented runbook is a common deficiency.
